chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Sitting in for Coleman Hawkins in Fletcher Henderson's band
summary: His wife called McRae to replace Hawkins one night at the Roseland, where they pulled out the hardest book he had seen.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Just don't read note for note. And this what helped me a lot in going through the bands. Like the night they called me to go down to (inaudible), take Coleman's place with Fletcher Henderson, it was the hardest book I ever saw in my life.
That happened one night back in the Charlie Johnson days (inaudible). That's when Fletcher had that tremendous band at the Roseland.
Willie (Inaudible) Smith -- all the top men in there, you know. His wife called me to come down. Coleman didn't show up that night.
Yeah, a lot of things in Concert B, I remember --
Yeah. The first thing they played --
Benny and I used to practice the clarinet

Benny Waters, yeah. Benny was a good clarinet man. So was we stayed with Ben Whittet, the first alto player (inaudible) --

Ben Whittet was a tremendous alto player and clarinet man. I think he came out of Hamilton Hampton. (inaudible). He was in the band now (inaudible). He could play -- he was a tremendous (inaudible). In fact, that whole band that Charlie had was a great band (inaudible). But Benny always told me, "Work on that clarinet."
